summary: self-sign ships a typosquat of `selfsigned` with an eval() backdoor in the exported generate() API
details: The package name `self-sign` mimics the widely used `selfsigned` module and its README uses `require('self-sign')`. The tarball contains `original.txt`, a verbatim copy of the upstream `selfsigned` source with the documented two-argument signature `exports.generate = async function generate(attrs, options)`. The shipped `index.js` is the same file modified to accept an undocumented third argument `defaults`: it strips `-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----` headers from that argument, base64-decodes the remainder, and passes the decoded string to `eval()`. Any consumer that calls `generate(attrs, options, defaults)` with an attacker-supplied third argument executes arbitrary JavaScript in the installer's Node.js process. The side-by-side presence of the clean upstream source and the tampered `index.js` documents that the eval sink was deliberately inserted, and the name/README mimicry indicates the package is positioned to be pulled in place of `selfsigned`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
